description: Which check guards which file. The single source for the coverage record: docs-testing.md points at this file instead of restating it, test/coverage.test.js keeps it honest, and AI/claude/hooks/name-covering-checks.mjs reads it to name the checks when a guarded file is edited. Paths are relative to the repository root.

test/smoke.test.js.what: The harness itself: both roles reach authenticated content, two sessions stay independent in either order, and the two sessions really are different users.

test/content.test.js.what: Wiring for the content suite: imports every check module so the whole suite runs in one process, and asserts that a run logs in once per role.

test/checks/permissions.js.what: Block-level and whole-file directives in both directions, including the admin directive and both plural aliases (teachers and students), their effect on the navigation tree, time-bounded windows, and the teacher-to-student downgrade. That the navigation tree and the page a link leads to agree for every file carrying a whole-file directive - the tree read from the rendered sidebar, the page from a direct request, compared against each other rather than against a derived expectation - and that the two refusals stay told apart by their cause. That a file a session may see reaches it without its directive line. That a rendered page costs the identity provider at most one account lookup however many directives it evaluates, and that a request evaluating no directive costs none - counted on the session by fetchAccount, because those lookups happen between the application and Keycloak where the browser cannot see them.

test/checks/views.js.what: The #exam, #practice and #answer pseudo-roles, driven through the ve and va preferences.

test/checks/rendering.js.what: Callouts and their collapsible forms, highlighted code, ==highlights== with and without one of the six colour emoji, fragment indices, side-by-side columns, the image forms, and the emitted PlantUML and Mermaid markup. That a page view is shown by its one owner with the value that defers to the stylesheets, and that the wait for it is bounded: a preference request left unanswered still produces a visible page and a console message naming what it waited for, while a page that came up normally reports nothing.

test/checks/legibility.js.what: What a rendered page presents to the person reading it, read off the page rather than out of a stylesheet: that nothing casts a shadow behind the prose or overrides the platform's rasterisation, that the page and document views declare a viewport laying the page out at the device's width without pinning the scale while the presentation view keeps its pinning, and that a 390px viewport really gets the narrow layout - the navigation folded away, the burger shown, and nothing pushing the page sideways. That every font family css/ names resolves to one this deployment declares, a generic, or a named system face, with the shipped names read from the @font-face block the renderer emitted rather than from a list kept in step by hand, and that a chain reaching for a shipped face ends in a generic. That the bar above the page, the navigation column and the menu render in one font. That inline code and a code block share one face at one size, both in fixed proportion to the reader's chosen size and following it when it changes, and that neither breaks a long token mid-word. That both themes clear WCAG AAA for body text as a measured ratio, and that the dark one is neither pure white nor at the maximum its background could reach. That a link in the text looks the same before and after it is followed, in both themes, and is underlined - the visited state computed from the page's own CSSOM, because Chrome answers getComputedStyle for a visited link with its unvisited style, and that computation held against the browser on the state the browser will report. That bold and italic on a rendered page are cuts this deployment ships rather than the browser's smear and shear: every file in the two font directories is read out of its own OS/2 table and held against the cut its name claims - the weight and the italic bit, through the sfnt, woff and woff2 containers the scanner accepts - and every family the renderer declares has a 700 face and an italic face, except the typefaces obsidian.js records as having none upstream. That the two chains applyAttributes() writes onto the page as inline styles begin at the family getFontImports() declared and end in the generic that typeface belongs to - a serif behind a serif, a monospace behind a monospace - which no stylesheet can supply, because an inline style outranks them all. That the deployment nominates the two typefaces a reader who has chosen none reads in, by name rather than by position: that each nomination is one the picker it belongs to actually offers - a nomination nobody offers is fallen past in silence onto whichever font sorts first - and that an attribute block carrying no font choice, which is what a reset account hands the page, resolves through the page's own chosenTypeface to those two rather than to a numeric default or to the alphabet. And that a position stored as a string rather than a number, as 20 of the accounts carrying preferences in the production realm did, falls to the nomination instead of being guessed at, because the page cannot tell a stringified position from the name of a font no longer shipped.

test/checks/navigation.js.what: Wiki-link resolution including the duplicated basename — with a digit in the name and without one — and the name with spaces, the folder-name edge cases, the table of contents and the navigation tree.
corpus: md/folder-tests/a very long folder with spaces oh my god i cannot believe how long it is/Untitled.md

test/checks/presentation.js.what: The deck built from the source's heading structure, fragments in a deck, the deck's own references including the known-dangling list, that it contacts no host but the application and the identity provider, that a host a stylesheet asks for is recorded even when refused, the document view, and the documented shortcut into it with the shift key held and without. That one corpus file opened in all three views becomes visible exactly once in each, by that view's own owner and with the value that defers to the stylesheets - read as the sequence of values the property takes, so a second script writing it fails the run.

test/checks/session-lifecycle.js.what: A session signed out at Keycloak while its page is open: the next click lands at the login, a sub-resource asked for with the ended session's cookie gets 401 instead of a redirect, and the application keeps running with every other session intact.

test/checks/attachments.js.what: Which session is served which attachment under /md, against a running instance: an attachment on an unrestricted page is served to everyone, one only in a teacher block to teachers only, one in several places as widely as the most visible of them, one only inside a closed window or only in the exam variant to nobody who cannot see that place, an ambiguous embed and an unreferenced file to nobody. That a teacher who switches to the student view loses what only the teacher view showed, grant included, that a refusal is answered exactly like a missing file (status, headers apart from the date, body), and that a served attachment is marked private. That every attachment any corpus page addresses for the test student and the test teacher is served by the full decision with the render-time grants dropped, which keeps the extractor and the renderer in step.

test/checks/pdf-embeds.js.what: Wiki links and embeds that name a PDF, in the page view, the presentation and the printable document: [[name.pdf]] and [[name.pdf|text]] render as links to the percent-encoded path and the PDF is served to a student (so the gate counts the wiki link as a reference), a wiki link in inline code stays as written, the sanitized page keeps the .sl-pdf placeholder with its data-* size, the page view upgrades it to an iframe served as application/pdf with the link beneath and the author's 600x400, the slide shows a visible viewer within the slide bounds that prevents swiping, and the document view shows the link and no viewer.

test/checks/deployment-surface.js.what: What a running instance publishes over HTTP: that keycloak.json, the application sources, the dependency manifests and what sits beside a mounted package directory are not served and a refusal looks like a path with no file behind it, that the assets a page addresses still are — including the ones only a stylesheet names — that every same-origin reference of a rendered page resolves in all three views, the assets from their mounts and the attachments under /md for the session the page was rendered for, and that the one endpoint answering before authentication survives a parameter it cannot interpret. That a page which cannot reach the reload stream keeps trying with a growing delay rather than on a fixed timer. That a self-authenticating route — the directory search endpoint and the status endpoint beside it — returns no directory data to a request carrying neither a bearer token nor, distinctly, to one carrying only a valid browser session. That no route fetches a URL a request names: the former /convert route, asked by GET and POST to fetch a local listener or render a posted body, makes no outbound request and is answered exactly like a path that never existed.

test/checks/directory-search.js.what: GET /api/admin/directory/search: a teacher token searching by name and by a role/group value that is not a class or teacher/admin, an admin token succeeding without holding teacher, a student token refused, a missing bearer refused, an invalidated (expired/revoked-shaped) token refused indistinguishably from a missing one, a match's response carrying only name, its two parts, the e-mail address and roles, and an empty or unmatched query answering with an empty list rather than an error. That a search the server cannot answer yet reports the running fetch (202) instead of being held open, and is answered once the caller repeats it. GET /api/admin/directory/status: a teacher token reading what the directory holds without transferring any of it, the payload carrying figures only and no record from the directory, and a student token refused indistinguishably from a request carrying no identity at all.

test/checks/search.js.what: What a search may return and what it may never reveal: that a term occurring only in a file whose first line restricts it, only in a restricted block, only in a block addressed to another person by name, or only across the seam a removed block leaves behind, comes back as nothing - and as the same nothing a term that is in no file at all comes back as. That the joined document really does contain the seam term, so the seam check is about a seam. That the same session running the same query before and after the teacher/student toggle sees its results change exactly as the rendered page does. That a file restricted after the last scan is not returned and one relaxed after it is, driven by editing the corpus while the application runs. That an answer carries the results and nothing else - no total, no mark for what was left out - and that every occurrence it reports is an occurrence the session can count on the page it is served. That following a result lands on its heading, that a repeated heading lands on the occurrence the search found, and that a hand-written target naming a heading the session may not see leaves the page at its top. That a query below the minimum length is refused, that a request carrying no session is refused, that matching is substring and case-insensitive, that a name or heading match outranks a body match, and that a whole query costs the identity provider at most one account lookup. That neither switch a reader may set for themselves opens the exam variant to them: a student that turns the exam view on, and a teacher that turns it on while in the student view, are told nothing about the `@@@ #exam` block, and every session is offered exactly one of the exam and practice variants across both roles and both settings. That `#answer` is a view and not a restriction - `va` alone decides it, for a student exactly as for a teacher - stated here so it is not mistaken for one. And that a block whose window has closed is found by nobody, the teacher session included, since a closed window is the one directive `admin` does not short-circuit, in both the block form the segment filter decides and the whole-file form `resolveFileVisibility` decides.

test/checks/search-keyboard.js.what: Driving the search from the keyboard: that arrow-down enters the list at its first result and stops at its last node without wrapping, that exactly one node carries the mark at a time and that the field names the same node it stands on, that arrow-right opens a result and then steps into its headings while arrow-down walks them and steps out to the result below, that arrow-left closes a heading list onto the result it belongs to and hands the selection back from a result that is not open, that arrow-up at the first result hands it back too and that arrow-left afterwards moves the caret within the query again. That arrow-right at the end of the query resumes the node the selection was handed back from while arrow-down starts at the top whatever happened earlier, that a further character typed forgets that node, and that anywhere but the end of the query arrow-right stays the caret - a selected query collapses, a caret inside it moves one character, and a query nothing answers has nothing to step into. That enter leaves the reader exactly where a pointer following the same node leaves them, compared against the click rather than against a rebuilt expectation, for a result and for a heading. That a click into the field selects the query it holds, that arrow-right then leaves the caret at its end so the next character extends it, and that a pointerdown carrying pointerType touch before the focus selects nothing. That entering the list, walking it and leaving it make no request to /search and leave the query alone, that a walk moves neither the caret within the query nor the page behind the sidebar, and that the Ctrl+Alt print shortcut still works with the caret in the field. That expanded is one state whichever of the chevron and the arrow keys set it, in both directions, and that a new answer - narrower, or below the minimum length - gives the selection up. The two shapes the walk needs are asserted before they are relied on, so a corpus edit fails the fixture rather than weakening the checks.

test/directive-grammar.test.js.what: What a permission directive means, entry by entry: a table of edge-case directive lines read by parseFirstLineForPermissions, covering the permissive cases of parseLocalDateTime that a hand-written mirror gets wrong. It is the oracle the companion plugin's own grammar is held against - the plugin's parseDirectiveEntries reads the same table and has to reach the same conclusion per entry, so a divergence fails here rather than misinforming a person writing a document. Needs no browser, no login and no server; it does need the plugin checkout the AI/plugin symlink points at.

test/semester-table.test.js.what: The dates a semester table is made of: the walk from the first lesson to the last, the weekdays it keeps, and the shape of the table written from them. Taken out of the plugin's own main.ts rather than reimplemented, so the check cannot drift away from the code it is about. Covers the cases that are invisible while writing it - both ends of the range, the daylight-saving switch a semester crosses twice, the turn of the month and of the year, and five timezones that have to produce one identical table because the corpus is shared. Also that the generated Markdown is a table to a GitHub-flavoured renderer, standalone and under a paragraph. Needs no browser, no login and no server; it does need the plugin checkout the AI/plugin symlink points at. What the command does to a document is in test/obsidian/plugin.test.js, which drives the real editor.

test/invitation-list.test.js.what: The text the plugin's "Invitation list…" command writes: the author's example format (prefix, fields joined by the field separator, postfix), addresses one per line and comma-joined with nothing after the last entry, \n and \t resolved in one left-to-right pass so \\n stays a backslash and an n, field order, surname order and a person chosen twice written once, the class as every class-like value joined by /, values written verbatim, a missing address written empty with its separators and counted, an instance that sends no addresses reported as such rather than counted, and a stored format read back with anything malformed replaced by the default. Taken out of the plugin's own main.ts rather than reimplemented. Needs no browser, no login and no server; it does need the plugin checkout the AI/plugin symlink points at.

test/section-names.test.js.what: The order the per-name commands write names in and the content each section starts with: chosen people by surname then given name in German collation (umlauts beside their base letter, case ignored, two-word surnames whole), a display-name fallback for an instance that sends no name parts, typed names after them in their own order; and the content given once for every section - blank stays the single blank line, one trailing line break is dropped, a line opening or closing a restriction is caught. Taken out of the plugin's own main.ts rather than reimplemented. Needs no browser, no login and no server; it does need the plugin checkout the AI/plugin symlink points at.

test/coverage.test.js.what: The coverage record itself: every path it names exists, every test file appears in it, and no entry names a file that is gone.

test/directory-service.test.js.what: A regression guard for the Keycloak admin-API pagination fix: fetchAllUserPages keeps asking for pages until one comes back short, rather than silently stopping at the first (a directory larger than one page going quietly missing past the 100th user). Stubs fetch; needs no live realm, no browser, no login.

test/permission-context.test.js.what: That a request resolves its permission context once: many checks of one request cause one account lookup, concurrent checks started before the first resolves cause one, and a request evaluating no directive causes none. That the downgraded check and the check beside it do not affect each other in either order, that a role inherited from Object.prototype - constructor, __proto__ - is granted to nobody, that a failed lookup settles the whole request on the default preferences with its roles intact and is logged once, and that every directive of one request is decided against the same reference time even when a window closes mid-request. Stubs fetch; needs no live realm, no browser, no login.

test/attachments.test.js.what: What a page addresses and which file that is: embeds with and without a size, Markdown images, links and definitions, raw img/video/audio/source/a attributes, external URLs and Markdown targets left out, references inside fenced or inline code ignored, an ambiguous basename resolving to nothing, relative paths against the page's folder, /md/ paths with percent-encoding, and paths that leave md/ rejected. Who is served an attachment by the full decision, case by case, including a removed reference and a file added after the page that embeds it. The unreferenced report: sorted paths, one log line each plus the count, replaced as a whole on rescan, and every listed path refused. The grant store: only same-origin attachments the body addresses, expiry and pruning, invalidation by a scan and by a preference write, and that app.js records grants in exactly one place, behind the corpus check. Scans a temporary fixture corpus and stubs fetch; needs no server, no browser, no login. Wiki links [[name]] as references of their own kind, resolved like embeds and never to a Markdown page, the renderer turning them into Markdown links to the encoded path (inline code left as written), and the PDF embed placeholder with its size surviving the sanitizer.

test/deployment-config.test.js.what: That every environment variable the application reads reaches a deployed instance through one of the two channels a deployment has - the image's own .env, written by the workflow and baked in by the Dockerfile, or the container's environment, written to deploy/.env and interpolated by docker-compose.yml - and that neither channel is wired up only halfway. Added after DIRECTORY_SERVICE_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET were read by the directory-search endpoint for two changes while nothing in the pipeline set them. That the exam module's switch EXAM_MODULE and the school's periods SCHOOL_PERIODS travel by the container's environment and not in the image, that the Dockerfile ships exam/, that EXAM_DB_PATH (the harness's own database) reaches no deployed instance, that the WYSIWYG templates run without the module (neither variable set) and mount no data volume, and that no static mount reaches the data directory, and that the Dockerfile ships i18n/, which every instance imports.

test/checks/exam-embedding.js.what: Embedded exam-module elements on an instance without the module: a teacher sees a notice per known element (also in the presentation and document views), a student and a teacher in student view see nothing, an unknown kind and the blocks' source never show, an example inside a longer fence stays text, the gradebook's results and gradebook blocks are a notice each for a teacher and nothing for a student, no page names the module's script or offers a teacher a button to it or requests /exam/, and every path under /exam/ answers as a path with nothing behind it.

test/exam.test.js.what: The instance with the exam module on, in a process of its own against a database created for the run and removed afterwards: the start-up log names that database and a fresh migration, /exam/api/me reports the identity and the student-view downgrade, an unauthenticated request is refused, the module page is shown to teachers in the instance's frame and to nobody else, the top bar offers a teacher (not a student, not a teacher in student view) a button to it, module pages use the whole width while content pages keep the reading column, elements mount as placeholders the client draws its frame into (teacher-only ones only for teachers), the presentation and document views and pages without elements load no module script, and the database is not retrievable over HTTP. Classes and courses against the demo realm: a teacher creates the current school year (twice is refused), ticks a roster from the directory's client-role class (exactly the ticked members, names from the directory), cannot put a teacher on a roster, removes a student who stays listed as left, creates a course once per class and subject however it is capitalized and saves weights only when they make 100 %, sees the class page drawn by the client, and every route of classes and courses refuses a student and a teacher in student view (403 for the API, nothing for the pages) without changing anything. The gradebook: results in columns for a roster of the shared student and a username the directory does not know become a proposal with an empty category left out, a result for someone off the roster or above the column's maximum is refused and the old batch route records nothing, the student sees the proposal, then the override instead of it, and the comment only once marked visible (through the API and on /exam/my), each result by its column's name, teachers see proposal and override side by side, every gradebook route - columns and cells included - refuses a student and a teacher in student view while the student's own route ignores any username it is given, and the fixture page draws the results for everyone and the gradebook for a teacher only, without a module bar. The sheet: the + of a category adds a column and the category heading spans its columns, online tests keep their heading with the weight before any test is written, a typed result is stored without a save action and the row's proposal follows, a refused value is marked with its reason while the stored one stays, emptying removes the result, the override is saved on change, one row at a time is marked, the left four columns keep their place while the sheet scrolls in its own wrapper, the arrow keys move down and up a column and right and left across columns (and a category boundary) only at a value's edge, save the field left and never change a + or −; the year view shows the winter grade beside the year proposal combined by the winter share, with the summer's columns only; the config sheet saves weights only at 100 %. The module bar: every teacher page carries it as first served, with the right values and links and the current year by default, choosing a class opens it and clears the course, a course created from the bar is chosen afterwards and a duplicate refused, and no bar reaches a student, a teacher in student view or anyone's Exams page. The question pool, imported beside the running instance from a trimmed export: a teacher browses the category tree and finds a question by its English text, the preview carries both languages, the correct answers and an image served by the module (image/png, private, no-store; 404 for none), the browser page draws tree, list and a preview with the correct answer marked, the image loaded and the language switchable, the module's home links to the pool even without a school year, and no student or teacher in student view reaches the pool's API, its page or an image, refused the same way whether the image exists or not. The bar's buttons: every teacher page carries Question pool and Online tests, linked with the bar's context, the current one marked, the context kept across both pages and a choice in the bar staying on them, and neither reaches a student, a teacher in student view or the student's Exams page. Online tests: without a course in the bar the browser offers no assembly, with one ticked questions become a test of that course whose page shows the snapshot with the correct answers marked and whose usage the browser shows, every test route refuses a student and a teacher in student view, and a started test can be renamed but not deleted or re-assembled. Writing: a student's list of open tests shows a sitting created, one whose window opens later and a deleted test without a reload; a student starts an open test on /exam/my (no bar), sees its image, saves each change at once, resumes after a reload with the saved answer and the server's time left, has two focus losses counted, submits after a second confirmation and sees points and grade only; no response of that session carries a correct flag, a position or a snapshot id, the image and the questions are refused afterwards, no second attempt starts. The submitted attempt is a read-only field of its test's column in the sheet (no input, no delete, header linking to the test, the arrow keys passing over it) and counts in the proposal and the student's own results. A second browser is refused and recorded until the teacher releases the attempt, which then binds the next browser; a write after the deadline is refused and the attempt submitted with what was saved; an attempt whose page is closed is submitted by the sweep at its deadline; another student's attempt answers 404 and a teacher cannot write a test. The live view: its stream refuses a request without a session and a student's, a start, a focus loss and a submission are pushed to the teacher's page while the unauthenticated hot-reload channel carries none of it, the view keeps updating from snapshots when the stream is given up, and a teacher who switches to the student view in another tab gets refused and the view empties. The question editor: no student or teacher in student view reaches its pages, its API, the upload or a staged upload, and nothing changes; a mismatch is refused with every problem and the answer named; a styled save is stored without style and script and an image from outside the module is refused; a written test's snapshot is unchanged after an edit and the second of two concurrent saves is refused; the editor opens from the preview with both languages filled in, shows a refused field at its place, and returns to the browser with the category chosen after a save; a new question from the browser's New question: the rich-text field makes bold and inline code, filters a pasted web page to words and basic formatting, uploads a pasted image and one from the image button, shows a PDF's refusal under the field, and stores them as two images of the question; a 20 MB upload and a PDF named .png are refused with the reason, an unsaved upload is gone after the purge; a new question's image is shown in the browser and in a test assembled from it; a used question cannot be deleted, is retired with its test and usage kept, refused in assembly and revived back, a fresh one is deleted with its answers and image; a duplicate category name, a move into the own subtree and a non-empty delete are refused, a moved question keeps its usage; and an unwritten test takes up an edit only through Update this test, with its questions in the same order, while a written one keeps its text and refuses the update. The question import: no student and no teacher in student view reaches the import page, the format description or any of its API routes, and the pool is unchanged; a broken file uploaded in the page lists its problems with line and question and a Copy problems button, offers no import and stores nothing; a clean file shows its preview with the categories to be created, imports on confirmation, and the browser opens with only the unreviewed questions, each with the stripe and badge; with a course in the bar a chosen unreviewed row shows both, the assembly counts the unreviewed chosen question, Mark as reviewed clears the mark and moves on to the next question, and an editor save clears it too; the same file is refused with its earlier import named, taking back is refused naming the question while it is in a test, then confirmed in the page deletes the questions and the category the import created, after which the same file is accepted again; the downloaded description is Markdown named safelearn-question-format.md and lists the current categories. Last, the instance is restarted against the same database and an attempt resumes with its saved answer and its browser binding. Then the school's periods: without SCHOOL_PERIODS the sitting form and every window are in clock times as before; a malformed value switches the module off while the reader keeps serving; with the school's list /exam/api/me carries the periods, the form schedules periods 3 to 4 as 10:00 to 11:45 Vienna time with each choice's times as tooltip and the to period never before the from period, the sittings of a test, the list of tests, the live view (its periods element kept while the time left counts) and the class screen show the periods with 10:00–11:45 as tooltip, switching to exact times carries the window over, and a sitting off the periods shows clock times and opens the form in exact times. Last, an admin's corrections: /exam/api/me tells an admin from a teacher; a teacher who is no admin cannot delete a written test (409), remove a question from it or delete an attempt (403, a student too) and is offered no such button; an admin removes a question from a written test in its page with a second click and the attempt is scored over the rest, deletes an attempt in the live view so the student counts as not started, and deletes a written test with its attempts. Last, the interface in the reader's language and format: a teacher with German sees German in the sidebar, the settings menu (language and format marked as chosen), the module bar and the gradebook's categories, with lang=de on the page; English with de-AT shows English labels and a column dated 20.10.2026, en-GB 20/10/2026; a date is saved typed as 21.10.2026 and picked in the calendar by keyboard (opening on the field's date, a day right and a week down, Enter), while 32.10.2026 is marked invalid with the format beside the field and nothing is saved; a student with English writes a test of the German course with the questions in lang=de and English controls; and at the 390px viewport in German neither the module bar nor the sheet's headings overflow. /exam/api/me carries lang and loc. The year change: a year not yet ended and the current year are not closed; a past year is closed on its overview by a second click; a closed year refuses an entry, a column, a course, a config sheet, a roster change and a rename with 409 and keeps every result, and its sheet and class page show a note with no field and no enabled control; the next year offers last year's class one level up with its roster ticked, and Create puts only the ticked people on it and copies the course without columns; the leavers' report counts and names nobody, a purge with other counts is refused, the first click only asks, and the second removes the leaver's records from the closed year while a student on a current roster keeps theirs, with counts only in the log.

test/exam-foundation.test.js.what: The exam module unit by unit, without browser or server: database creation with WAL and foreign keys, migrations one transaction each with rollback on failure, refusal of a newer schema without touching the file, refusal of a read-only directory, a malformed SCHOOL_PERIODS disabling the module before any database is opened, pre-migration and daily VACUUM INTO copies that open on their own and their retention, the teacher/student gates including the student-view downgrade and switching back, the identity key, the embedding hooks (defaults, unknown kinds, nested fences, parameters, escaping, survival through DOMPurify, the presentation/document defaults), start-up failure disabling the module, and a throwing module request failing alone.

test/exam-classes.test.js.what: Classes and courses unit by unit, without browser or server: the first school year becomes current and exactly one is, a year's name and date order, a year and a class per year existing once; a 5th-year class whose checklist offers all 70 members of its unit (no teacher or admin) and whose roster holds the 25 ticked, nobody on a class unless ticked, a class name of letters and digits; the directory changing later leaving the roster alone and a name refresh changing names only; a student changing class mid-year kept and marked as left in one and on the other from then on, coming back clearing the mark, twice on a roster refused, an unknown username added as it is; the checklist sorted by name in German collation without roles, class names among the role values, the whole-directory search; a course once per class and subject however it is capitalized, its language, and config-sheet weights that are whole percentages making 100; and the indexes the classes migration adds.

test/exam-gradebook.test.js.what: The gradebook unit by unit, without browser or server: the scale's thresholds with the better grade on a threshold and rounding to four decimals before comparing, category means, the weighted mean with empty categories left out and the rest renormalized, no proposal without entries or with weightless categories only, the 0.815 → 2 example, each semester over the entries dated in it (the summer over summer entries only), a grade's band midpoint and its moving with the scale, the year proposal by the winter share (50, 40, 0 and 100 %) with either side missing; the migration from schema 3, grouping entries into one column per course, kind, date, maximum and note (a student's second result in a group in a column of its own) with every result, proposal and override unchanged and no temporary table left; columns as points out of a maximum, percent and +/−, a column named by its date, malformed or out-of-year columns and malformed, off-roster or above-maximum results refused, two results in one column replacing each other, emptying a field, renaming and re-dating, a new maximum recomputing or refused below a stored result, points and percent not switched while results exist, deleting a column with its results, and the sheet's column order per semester;
